parts.text: Let me run a query to confirm the revenue drop and get the overall picture for Q2 vs Q3 1995. I'll use the lineitem table which has revenue (l_extendedprice), and join with orders to get order dates.

input.query:
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate) as quarter,
    SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o_orderkey) as order_count,
    AVG(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as avg_line_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN lineitem l ON o.o_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
WHERE o_orderdate >= '1995-01-01' AND o_orderdate < '1996-01-01'
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate)
ORDER BY quarter

queries.query:
SELECT 
    c_mktsegment,
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate) as quarter,
    SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o_orderkey) as order_count
FROM orders o
JOIN lineitem l ON o.o_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
WHERE o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' AND o_orderdate < '1995-10-01'
GROUP BY c_mktsegment, DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate)
ORDER BY c_mktsegment, quarter

SELECT 
    n_name as region,
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate) as quarter,
    SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN lineitem l ON o.o_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
JOIN nation n ON c.c_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
WHERE o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' AND o_orderdate < '1995-10-01'
GROUP BY n_name, DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate)
ORDER BY n_name, quarter

SELECT 
    p_brand,
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate) as quarter,
    SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as revenue,
    COUNT(*) as line_count
FROM orders o
JOIN lineitem l ON o.o_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
JOIN part p ON l.l_partkey = p.p_partkey
WHERE o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' AND o_orderdate < '1995-10-01'
GROUP BY p_brand, DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o_orderdate)
ORDER BY p_brand, quarter

queries.query:
SELECT 
    c_mktsegment,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' AND o_orderdate < '1995-07-01' THEN l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) ELSE 0 END) as q2_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o_orderdate >= '1995-07-01' AND o_orderdate < '1995-10-01' THEN l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) ELSE 0 END) as q3_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' AND o_orderdate < '1995-07-01' THEN l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) ELSE 0 END) - 
    SUM(CASE WHEN o_orderdate >= '1995-07-01' AND o_orderdate < '1995-10-01' THEN l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) ELSE 0 END) as revenue_drop
FROM orders o
JOIN lineitem l ON o.o_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
GROUP BY c_mktsegment
ORDER BY revenue_drop DESC

WITH supplier_q2q3 AS (
    SELECT 
        supplier.s_name,
        supplier_nation.n_name AS supplier_nation,
        EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) AS quarter,
        SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) AS revenue
    FROM lineitem
    JOIN supplier ON lineitem.l_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
    JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
    JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
    JOIN nation ON customer.c_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
    JOIN nation AS supplier_nation ON supplier.s_nationkey = supplier_nation.n_nationkey
    WHERE nation.n_name = 'GERMANY'
      AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
    GROUP BY supplier.s_name, supplier_nation.n_name, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
)
SELECT 
    s.s_name,
    s.supplier_nation,
    q2.revenue AS q2_revenue,
    q3.revenue AS q3_revenue,
    q3.revenue - q2.revenue AS change,
    ROUND((q3.revenue - q2.revenue) / q2.revenue * 100, 1) AS pct_change
FROM supplier_q2q3 q2
JOIN supplier_q2q3 q3 ON q2.s_name = q3.s_name AND q2.supplier_nation = q3.supplier_nation
WHERE q2.quarter = 2 AND q3.quarter = 3
ORDER BY (q3.revenue - q2.revenue) ASC
LIMIT 15

input.query:
-- Get top 10 struggling suppliers from Germany Q2->Q3
WITH top10 AS (
    SELECT supplier.s_suppkey
    FROM lineitem
    JOIN supplier ON lineitem.l_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
    JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
    JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
    JOIN nation ON customer.c_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
    WHERE nation.n_name = 'GERMANY'
      AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
    GROUP BY supplier.s_suppkey, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
    HAVING SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) > 0
),
supplier_q2q3 AS (
    SELECT 
        supplier.s_suppkey,
        supplier.s_name,
        supplier_nation.n_name AS supplier_nation,
        nation.n_name AS customer_nation,
        EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) AS quarter,
        SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) AS revenue
    FROM lineitem
    JOIN supplier ON lineitem.l_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
    JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
    JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
    JOIN nation ON customer.c_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
    JOIN nation AS supplier_nation ON supplier.s_nationkey = supplier_nation.n_nationkey
    WHERE supplier.s_suppkey IN (SELECT s_suppkey FROM top10)
      AND nation.n_name != 'GERMANY'  -- Exclude Germany
      AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
    GROUP BY supplier.s_suppkey, supplier.s_name, supplier_nation.n_name, nation.n_name, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
)
SELECT 
    q2.s_name,
    q2.supplier_nation,
    q2.customer_nation,
    COALESCE(q2.revenue, 0) AS q2_revenue,
    COALESCE(q3.revenue, 0) AS q3_revenue,
    COALESCE(q3.revenue, 0) - COALESCE(q2.revenue, 0) AS change,
    CASE WHEN q2.revenue > 0 THEN ROUND((q3.revenue - q2.revenue) / q2.revenue * 100, 1) ELSE NULL END AS pct_change
FROM supplier_q2q3 q2
FULL OUTER JOIN supplier_q2q3 q3 ON q2.s_suppkey = q3.s_suppkey AND q2.customer_nation = q3.customer_nation AND q2.quarter = 2 AND q3.quarter = 3
ORDER BY q2.s_name, q2.customer_nation

      AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
    GROUP BY supplier.s_suppkey, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
    HAVING SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) > 0
),
supplier_q2q3 AS (
    SELECT 
        supplier.s_suppkey,
        supplier.s_name,
        supplier_nation.n_name AS supplier_nation,
        nation.n_name AS customer_nation,
        EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) AS quarter,
        SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) AS revenue

FROM supplier_q2q3 q2
FULL OUTER JOIN supplier_q2q3 q3 ON q2.s_suppkey = q3.s_suppkey AND q2.customer_nation = q3.customer_nation AND q2.quarter = 2 AND q3.quarter = 3

Let me query to find what product types the top 10 struggling German suppliers provide, focusing on Q2 vs Q3, and also break down by region to see the Germany/Europe drop.

First, let me identify the top 10 struggling suppliers (German suppliers with Q2->Q3 revenue drop), then see what product types they supply.

input.query:
-- Find product types for top 10 struggling German suppliers, Q2 vs Q3, by customer region
WITH struggling_suppliers AS (
    SELECT supplier.s_suppkey
    FROM lineitem
    JOIN supplier ON lineitem.l_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
    JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
    JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
    JOIN nation ON customer.c_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
    WHERE nation.n_name = 'GERMANY'
      AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
    GROUP BY supplier.s_suppkey, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
    HAVING SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) > 0
)
SELECT 
    p.p_type,
    nation.n_name AS customer_nation,
    region.r_name AS customer_region,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) AS quarter,
    SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) AS revenue
FROM lineitem
JOIN part ON lineitem.l_partkey = part.p_partkey
JOIN supplier ON lineitem.l_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
JOIN nation ON customer.c_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
JOIN region ON nation.n_regionkey = region.r_regionkey
WHERE supplier.s_suppkey IN (SELECT s_suppkey FROM struggling_suppliers)
  AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
GROUP BY p.p_type, nation.n_name, region.r_name, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
ORDER BY p_type, customer_region, quarter

The user wants to check discount levels for the struggling German suppliers' products in Q2 vs Q3. I should run a query to analyze discount patterns.

Let me build a query that shows average discounts by supplier and quarter for those German suppliers we identified earlier.

input.query:
-- Discount levels for German suppliers' products in Q2 vs Q3
WITH struggling_suppliers AS (
    SELECT supplier.s_suppkey
    FROM lineitem
    JOIN supplier ON lineitem.l_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
    JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
    JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
    JOIN nation ON customer.c_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
    WHERE nation.n_name = 'GERMANY'
      AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
    GROUP BY supplier.s_suppkey, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
    HAVING SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) > 0
)
SELECT 
    supplier.s_suppkey,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) AS quarter,
    COUNT(*) AS line_count,
    AVG(lineitem.l_discount) AS avg_discount,
    SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * lineitem.l_discount) AS discount_total
FROM lineitem
JOIN supplier ON lineitem.l_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
WHERE supplier.s_suppkey IN (SELECT s_suppkey FROM struggling_suppliers)
  AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) IN (2, 3)
GROUP BY supplier.s_suppkey, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate)
ORDER BY supplier.s_suppkey, quarter

parts.text:
The user wants to see revenue change between Q2 and Q3 for all European nations. I need to query the revenue for each European nation in Q2 and Q3, then calculate the change.

Let me write a query that:
1. Gets all nations in EUROPE region
2. Calculates revenue (lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) for Q2 and Q3 per nation
3. Shows the change between Q2 and Q3

I'll need to join: lineitem -> orders -> customer -> nation -> region, filter for EUROPE region.

input.query:
-- European nations Q2 vs Q3 revenue comparison
SELECT 
    nation.n_name AS nation,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) = 2 
        THEN lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount) ELSE 0 END) AS q2_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) = 3 
        THEN lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount) ELSE 0 END) AS q3_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) = 3 
        THEN lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount) ELSE 0 END) -
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) = 2 
        THEN lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount) ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_change
FROM lineitem
JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
JOIN nation ON customer.c_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
JOIN region ON nation.n_regionkey = region.r_regionkey
WHERE region.r_name = 'EUROPE'
GROUP BY nation.n_name
ORDER BY revenue_change DESC

parts.text:
The user wants to know if there were pricing changes for the parts from the previous query (Germany AUTOMOBILE parts in Q2) between Q2 and Q3. I need to compare pricing between these two quarters.

Let me look at the schema first to understand what tables and columns are available.

Now I need to check pricing changes between Q2 and Q3 for the Germany AUTOMOBILE parts. I need to look at:
1. The parts ordered in Q2 (which I already saw)
2. Check if those same parts have different pricing in Q3

Let me query the parts table to get the retail prices, then compare Q2 vs Q3 pricing. But wait - the lineitem table has l_extendedprice which is the actual transaction price, while the part table has p_retailprice which is the list price.

Let me compare average transaction prices in Q2 vs Q3 for the same parts in Germany AUTOMOBILE segment.

input.query:
-- Compare pricing between Q2 and Q3 for Germany AUTOMOBILE parts
-- Uses transaction price (extendedprice) from lineitem
WITH q2_pricing AS (
    SELECT 
        part.p_partkey,
        part.p_name,
        part.p_type,
        part.p_mfgr,
        AVG(lineitem.l_extendedprice) AS avg_price_q2,
        SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) AS total_revenue_q2,
        COUNT(*) AS order_count_q2
    FROM lineitem
    JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
    JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
    JOIN nation customer_nation ON customer.c_nationkey = customer_nation.n_nationkey
    JOIN part ON lineitem.l_partkey = part.p_partkey
    WHERE customer_nation.n_name = 'GERMANY'
        AND customer.c_mktsegment = 'AUTOMOBILE'
        AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) = 2
    GROUP BY part.p_partkey, part.p_name, part.p_type, part.p_mfgr
),
q3_pricing AS (
    SELECT 
        part.p_partkey,
        part.p_name,
        part.p_type,
        part.p_mfgr,
        AVG(lineitem.l_extendedprice) AS avg_price_q3,
        SUM(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount)) AS total_revenue_q3,
        COUNT(*) AS order_count_q3
    FROM lineitem
    JOIN orders ON lineitem.l_orderkey = orders.o_orderkey
    JOIN customer ON orders.o_custkey = customer.c_custkey
    JOIN nation customer_nation ON customer.c_nationkey = customer_nation.n_nationkey
    JOIN part ON lineitem.l_partkey = part.p_partkey
    WHERE customer_nation.n_name = 'GERMANY'
        AND customer.c_mktsegment = 'AUTOMOBILE'
        AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM orders.o_orderdate) = 3
    GROUP BY part.p_partkey, part.p_name, part.p_type, part.p_mfgr
)
SELECT 
    q2.p_name,
    q2.p_type,
    q2.avg_price_q2,
    q3.avg_price_q3,
    q3.avg_price_q2 - q2.avg_price_q2 AS price_change,
    ROUND(100.0 * (q3.avg_price_q2 - q2.avg_price_q2) / q2.avg_price_q2, 2) AS pct_change,
    q2.total_revenue_q2,
    q3.total_revenue_q3
FROM q2_pricing q2
FULL OUTER JOIN q3_pricing q3 ON q2.p_partkey = q3.p_partkey
ORDER BY ABS(q3.avg_price_q2 - q2.avg_price_q2) DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 30

parts.text:
The user wants to see which weeks had the biggest revenue drop. I need to calculate week-over-week revenue changes and find the biggest drops.

Let me run a query that calculates the weekly revenue and then finds the week-over-week change.

input.query:
WITH weekly_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('week', o.o_orderdate) AS week,
        SUM(o.o_totalprice) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
    JOIN nation cust_n ON c.c_nationkey = cust_n.n_nationkey
    WHERE o.o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' 
      AND o.o_orderdate < '1995-10-01'
      AND cust_n.n_regionkey != 1
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('week', o.o_orderdate)
)
SELECT 
    week,
    revenue,
    LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY week) AS prev_week_revenue,
    revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY week) AS revenue_change,
    ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY week)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY week) * 100, 2) AS pct_change
FROM weekly_revenue
ORDER BY revenue_change ASC
LIMIT 10

The user is asking what was happening with suppliers during those worst weeks. Let me analyze this data:

The 5 worst weeks (by revenue) were:
- 1995-04-24 (early April - shows as 1995-03-27 due to ship dates which is a week before)
- 1995-07-17 
- 1995-07-31
- 1995-08-28 (the worst - 54.8% drop)
- 1995-09-18 (shows as 1995-09-25)

Now, looking at the supplier nation breakdown for these weeks, I need to find patterns, especially around the worst week (Aug 28).

For the week of Aug 28 (the worst week):
- Vietnam: $680K (highest)
- Kenya: $542K
- United States: $495K
- United Kingdom: $466K
- Egypt: $459K
- Mozambique: $356K

The supplier distribution seems fairly even across nations, so let me look at whether there were any supply issues - maybe comparing to prior weeks.

Let me provide a concise analysis.

Here's the supplier breakdown during those 5 worst weeks:

| Week (Ship Date) | Top Supplier Nation | Revenue | 2nd Place | Revenue |
|-----------------|---------------------|---------|------------|---------|
| **Aug 28** (worst) | Vietnam | $681K | Kenya | $542K |
| Jul 31 | United States | $638K | Russia | $605K |
| Jul 17 | China | $440K | Mozambique | $388K |
| Apr 24* | Germany | $556K | United States | $472K |
| Sep 18* | Indonesia | $685K | India | $587K |

*Note: Ship dates offset from order dates

**Key observations for the worst week (Aug 28):**
- Vietnam led with $681K in supplier revenue, followed by Kenya ($542K) and United States ($495K)
- All major supplier nations were active - no obvious supply chain failure
- The drop was broad-based across nearly all supplier nations, not isolated to specific regions
- Compared to Jul 31: US dropped $143K (22%), UK dropped $145K (31%), Egypt also dropped significantly

There wasn't a single supplier nation causing the issue - it appears to be a broad demand-side drop rather than supply constraints. The supplier nations remained active but orders simply dropped off.

The first query failed, but I got results from the other three. Let me fix the first query and get the weekly metrics. Actually, let me check what the issue was - it seems like there was a typo in the query where I was trying to cross join. Let me rewrite that query to get the weekly metrics comparison between prior period and worst weeks.

I got results for:
1. Top affected regions (supplier nations) - showing ~99.8% drops (which seems odd - probably because I'm comparing different time periods incorrectly)
2. Top affected suppliers - showing 97-98% drops
3. Churned customers - showing only 2 customers churned

Let me fix the first query and get weekly metrics. Also, I should reconsider the analysis - comparing prior 6-month period to 5 weeks seems like an apples-to-oranges comparison which is why we're seeing such dramatic drops.

input.query:
WITH worst_weeks AS (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', o.o_orderdate) AS week
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
    JOIN nation cust_n ON c.c_nationkey = cust_n.n_nationkey
    WHERE o.o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' AND o.o_orderdate < '1995-10-01' AND cust_n.n_regionkey != 1
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('week', o.o_orderdate)
    ORDER BY SUM(o.o_totalprice) ASC
    LIMIT 5
),
avg_prior_week AS (
    SELECT AVG(weekly_rev) AS avg_weekly_revenue
    FROM (
        SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', o.o_orderdate) AS week, SUM(o.o_totalprice) AS weekly_rev
        FROM orders o
        JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
        JOIN nation cust_n ON c.c_nationkey = cust_n.n_nationkey
        WHERE o.o_orderdate >= '1994-10-01' AND o.o_orderdate < '1995-04-01' AND cust_n.n_regionkey != 1
        GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('week', o.o_orderdate)
    )
)
SELECT 
    w.week,
    SUM(o.o_totalprice) AS week_revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.o_orderkey) AS order_count,
    (SELECT avg_weekly_revenue FROM avg_prior_week) AS prior_avg_weekly_rev,
    ROUND(((SELECT avg_weekly_revenue FROM avg_prior_week) - SUM(o.o_totalprice)) / (SELECT avg_weekly_revenue FROM avg_prior_week) * 100, 1) AS pct_below_avg
FROM orders o
JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
JOIN nation cust_n ON c.c_nationkey = cust_n.n_nationkey
WHERE o.o_orderdate >= '1995-04-01' AND o.o_orderdate < '1995-10-01' AND cust_n.n_regionkey != 1
GROUP BY w.week
ORDER BY w.week

WITH churned AS (
    SELECT c.c_custkey
    FROM customer c
    JOIN nation cust_n ON c.c_nationkey = cust_n.n_nationkey

        GROUP BY c.c_custkey
    ) po ON c.c_custkey = po.c_custkey
)

The user is asking for a final report with four key sections: weekly metrics, top affected regions, top affected suppliers, and churned customer impact. Looking at the context, I need to provide a summary report based on the query results I've gathered. Let me synthesize the findings:

input.query:
SELECT 
    s.s_suppkey,
    s.s_name,
    n.n_name AS nation,
    SUM(l.l_extendedprice * (1 - l.l_discount)) AS revenue
FROM lineitem l
JOIN orders o ON l.l_orderkey = o.o_orderkey
JOIN customer c ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
JOIN supplier s ON l.l_suppkey = s.s_suppkey
JOIN nation n ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
JOIN region r ON n.n_regionkey = r.r_regionkey
WHERE 
    l.l_shipdate >= '1995-04-01'

    AND c.c_nationkey IN (SELECT n_nationkey FROM nation WHERE n_regionkey != 1)
    AND r.r_name != 'AMERICA'
GROUP BY s.s_suppkey, s.s_name, n.n_name
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
